<!-- ROW 1 — question and idea, one section -->
::: {.card title="Incompatibility as a single interference signal"}
:::: {.poster-grid widths="1fr, 1.6fr"}

::: {.col}
::: {.placeholder height="10cm"}
The question in 3–4 lines: when are two measurements compatible? Standard route (tomography → SDP) scales with $d$; the switch route gives one number, independent of $d$.
:::
:::

::: {.col}
::: {.placeholder height="10cm"}
The idea in one picture: eigenbases of $A$, $B$ → [$\mathcal{A}$ then $\mathcal{B}$]{.ab} and [$\mathcal{B}$ then $\mathcal{A}$]{.ba} in superposition → interference on the control → $p_-$ → MED.
:::
:::

::::
:::

::: {.card title="Photonic implementation"}

One intro line: the system is the polarization qubit of a heralded single photon.
